City opens a library in an old tram depot

By Grace Hopper, Culture correspondent

A tram depot that stood empty for thirty years reopened on Saturday as the city's largest public library. The terminal has outlived almost every interface that came after it. It is fast, it is scriptable, and it never asks you to wait for a spinner.

Reading on the web, by contrast, has become a negotiation with banners, overlays and autoplaying video. The words are in there somewhere. A reader view strips a page down to the text its author wrote, then sets it in a column narrow enough that the eye can find the next line without effort.

"We wanted somewhere people could just sit," said the head librarian. Typography in a grid of fixed cells is constrained, but the constraints are old friends: bold, italic, underline, and a handful of colours carry a long way.

The library is open every day from nine. Related: why one writer reads in a terminal.
